methods: Read exact changed Objective-C owner/FFI and Rust callback boundary.

findings: Accepted start transfers sole reply-context ownership to native finish; rejected start never calls back and Rust reclaims its Box. finish nulls context before callback, preventing reentrant duplicate release.

Cancel matches browser plus operation token, sets retired before callback, clears observation identity, and keeps execution slot until exact completion. Zero/unmatched cancellation cannot retire another request.
Manual activity uses the same retirement separation. Close clears ownership before callbacks; stale callbacks cannot clear a replacement view/request.
Read/observation/snapshot callback paths check exact identity and retired state before publishing content or an observation.
Peer actual fixed-JS canary demonstrates a late page effect after cancellation while successor observation remains blocked. This supports unknown-effect wording rather than abort claims.
classification: Baseline has 35/38 raw passes. One of three failed assertions expected an unsafe immediate successor despite unconfirmed native execution; receipt explicitly corrects that expectation and retains original bytes. It is not counted as an additional product defect. Original compile errors are probe-only and preserved.
